page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Reduce both angles to 20°
steps.margin_note: First mark. 290° = 360° − 70° keeps the cosine positive; 250° = 180° + 70° makes the sine negative. Complementary angles then turn both into ratios of 20°.

recall.must_convey: That cos290° = sin20° and sin250° = −cos20°, so the left side becomes 1/sin20° − 1/(√3 cos20°).
accept: two ninety is three sixty minus seventy so the cosine stays positive
two fifty is one eighty plus seventy so the sine is negative
cos two ninety is sin twenty and sin two fifty is minus cos twenty
rendu angles ni twenty degrees ki reduce chestham

steps.why: Both angles sit 70° away from a standard direction, so both reduce to a ratio of 20°. Working with one angle instead of two is what makes the rest short.

steps.label: Combine the two fractions
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Take out a 2 from the numerator to see sin(60° − 20°), and use 2 sin20° cos20° = sin40° in the denominator, so sin40° cancels.
steps.memory_tip: √3 cos20° − sin20° = 2 sin(60° − 20°) = 2 sin40°, and the bottom carries sin40° too.

recall.must_convey: That the numerator is 2 sin40° and the denominator (√3/2) sin40°, so sin40° cancels and 4/√3 is left.
accept: take the two out and the top is two sin forty
the bottom is root three by two times sin forty
sin forty cancels and two divided by root three by two is four by root three
top two sin forty, bottom root three by two sin forty, cancel cheste four by root three
the answer is four by root three

steps.why: √3 cos20° − sin20° is 2 times the expansion of sin(60° − 20°), because sin60° = √3/2 and cos60° = 1/2. Taking the 2 out first is what makes that visible.
common_mistakes: Cancelling sin40° before writing the 2 and the √3/2.
Forgetting the 2 in 2 sin20° cos20° = sin40°.
